tagging_basis: OCR H432 numbered specification sections (lettered learning outcomes as evidence)

units.label: 1(a)(i)
units.summary: Explain the large boiling point difference between ammonia and ammonium nitrate.
units.difficulty_basis: Compare simple molecular and ionic bonding

units.label: 1(a)(ii)
units.summary: Decide whether the two nitrogen atoms in ammonium nitrate have the same oxidation number.
units.difficulty_basis: Straightforward oxidation number assignment

units.label: 1(b)(i)
units.summary: Read the percentage composition of copper and zinc from a mass spectrum.
units.difficulty_basis: Simple data reading from labelled peaks

units.label: 1(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the relative atomic mass of zinc from its isotope abundances in the spectrum.
units.difficulty_basis: Weighted mean with rescaling to zinc only

units.label: 1(c)(i)
units.summary: Predict proton NMR splitting patterns for four proton environments in a given molecule.
units.difficulty_basis: Applies n+1 rule to unfamiliar molecule

units.label: 1(c)(ii)
units.summary: Suggest why two proton environments have particular chemical shift values.
units.difficulty_basis: Link shifts to neighbouring carbonyl groups

units.label: 1(d)(i)
units.summary: State and explain the different H-N-H bond angles in two amino acid salts.
units.difficulty_basis: Electron pair repulsion with lone pair comparison

units.label: 1(d)(ii)
units.summary: Write an equation and draw both square planar isomers of copper(II) glycinate.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar bidentate complex with isomer drawing

units.label: 2(a)(i)
units.summary: Calculate the concentration of calcium hypochlorite from a chlorine gas volume in standard form.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step with gas volume and sig figs

units.label: 2(a)(ii)
units.summary: Write the decomposition equation of calcium hypochlorite and explain the disproportionation by oxidation numbers.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar equation plus oxidation number argument

units.label: 2(b)
units.summary: Explain with electrode potentials and equilibrium how chromium species act as oxidising or reducing agents.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended argument combining E values and equations

units.label: 2(c)
units.summary: Construct the equation for hydrogen sulfide reacting with acidified permanganate.
units.difficulty_basis: Unfamiliar redox equation needs half-equations

units.label: 3(a)
units.summary: Draw reflux apparatus, calculate percentage yield of 1-bromobutane and describe purification.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended practical and calculation response

units.label: 3(b)
units.summary: Show both steps of the mechanism of butan-1-ol with bromide ions and acid.
units.difficulty_basis: Two step mechanism with protonation

units.label: 4(a)
units.summary: Explain different initial rates at two temperatures and deduce the sign of the enthalpy change from absorbance data.
units.difficulty_basis: Graph interpretation combining rate and equilibrium

units.label: 4(b)(i)
units.summary: Explain why chloride concentration drops sharply when silver nitrate is added.
units.difficulty_basis: Single recall of precipitation

units.label: 4(b)(ii)
units.summary: Explain the changes in cobalt complex and chloride concentrations after silver nitrate is added.
units.difficulty_basis: Equilibrium shift with stoichiometric links

units.label: 5(a)
units.summary: Process calorimetry data and use an energy cycle to find the hydration enthalpy of calcium ions.
units.difficulty_basis: Extended multi-stage calculation with cycle

units.label: 5(b)(i)
units.summary: Write the complete combustion equation for a 1:1 mole mixture of octane and ethanol.
units.difficulty_basis: Combined fuel equation needs careful balancing

units.label: 5(b)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the energy released by burning 8.00 kg of an octane and ethanol blend.
units.difficulty_basis: Needs mole ratio from mass of mixed fuel

units.label: 6(a)
units.summary: State the total number of optical isomers of vitamin C from its structure.
units.difficulty_basis: Count chiral centres then apply 2 to the n

units.label: 6(b)(i)
units.summary: Suggest why vitamin C is extremely soluble in water.
units.difficulty_basis: Single recall of hydrogen bonding

units.label: 6(b)(ii)
units.summary: Determine x and y in the carboxylic acid that forms the vitamin C ester.
units.difficulty_basis: Formula subtraction after esterification

units.label: 6(c)(i)
units.summary: Add curly arrows showing vitamin C donating a proton to water.
units.difficulty_basis: Mechanism of proton transfer

units.label: 6(c)(ii)
units.summary: Calculate the pH of a vitamin C solution using the acid dissociation constant.
units.difficulty_basis: Weak acid calculation with concentration scaling

units.label: 6(d)
units.summary: Calculate the mass of vitamin C in a serving of orange juice from an iodine titration.
units.difficulty_basis: Multi-step titration with dilution scaling
